summary: Phase 55.11j — Tested reset_admin_password.py. 10/11 pytest tests pass. CRITICAL BUG confirmed: script writes to password_hash/hashed_password but /api/auth/login reads user['password']. After reset, login STILL returns 401. Admin login currently works only because admin's `password` field already has a valid bcrypt hash (unrelated to the script). Baseline admin login (admin@vhc.in / VhcAdmin@2024) returns 200 without any script run.

critical.issue: Script writes bcrypt hash to password_hash & hashed_password only, but routes/auth.py:183 reads user['password']. After running the script on a user with empty password field, POST /api/auth/login returns HTTP 401 'Invalid credentials'. The emergency fix does NOT actually restore login. Fix: in reset_password(), add 'password': new_hash to the $set dict (alongside password_hash & hashed_password).

action_items: In /app/backend/scripts/reset_admin_password.py::reset_password, add "password": new_hash to the update $set (alongside password_hash / hashed_password) so the field the login route actually reads is updated. Without this the emergency script is a no-op for login recovery.
Optional: audit for any other legacy code paths that still read password_hash / hashed_password. If none, the script can write ONLY 'password'; if some do, writing all three is fine.
Consider updating /app/memory/PRD or a runbook noting the canonical field name is `password` (not `password_hash`).
critical_code_review_comments: reset_admin_password.py mismatch with login route field name — see critical bug above. This is the whole reason for phase 55.11j; the script as-shipped will not restore prod admin login.
Script assumes password field naming convention that does not match the codebase (routes/auth.py, seed_users.py all use `password`).
_get_db() uses tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=True — acceptable for emergency script but flag for security review.
Script does not log to a file (only stdout) — for prod emergency ops consider structured logging.
test_credentials: admin@vhc.in / VhcAdmin@2024 — verified working via POST /api/auth/login (baseline test passes without any script intervention)
seed_data_creation: Test seeds RESET_TEST_<label>_<uuid>@example.com users; final cleanup test deletes all RESET_TEST_ users. Admin@vhc.in was NEVER modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent adds `'password': new_hash` to update dict in reset_admin_password.py::reset_password, re-run: cd /app/backend && python3 -m pytest tests/test_reset_admin_password.py -v. test_login_endpoint_after_reset must go green. Do NOT reset admin@vhc.in — its `password` field already has a valid bcrypt hash and login currently works.
rca_of_the_issue: RCA: The login endpoint /api/auth/login (backend/routes/auth.py line 183) authenticates via `verify_password(credentials.password, user['password'])` — it looks up the `password` field. The new script writes ONLY `password_hash` and `hashed_password`. Confirmed by direct MongoDB inspection: admin@vhc.in doc has key `password` (60-char bcrypt string) and no `password_hash`/`hashed_password` at all. Reproduction: seed user with empty `password`, run script with any password X, then POST /api/auth/login {email, X} → 401. Mitigation: one-line fix in reset_password() to include `'password': new_hash` in the $set. Also verified the reset_admin script did NOT actually fix admin login on prod — login likely worked before because admin's `password` field was still populated; the empty `password_hash` observation was misleading (it's a vestigial field the login route never consulted).
